article_notes: 32 PCR-confirmed naturally infected dogs (Chennai, India): 8 B. vogeli, 12 B. gibsoni, 12 mixed B. vogeli + B. gibsoni; 14 non-survivors and 18 survivors followed during the treatment period (no fixed horizon stated). Blood taken on admission before treatment. Survivor vs non-survivor comparisons are given only in the text and in Figures 1-5 (bar charts not in the Markdown), so no group means or exact p-values are available for them; rows use the p thresholds stated in the text. One-way ANOVA with Tukey's test across control, survivors and non-survivors. UIBC: the text reports only comparisons with controls, so the survivor vs non-survivor result is unclear. Not extracted: Table 2 (markers compared between species groups B. vogeli / B. gibsoni / mixed; species groups are not a severity definition) and Table 3 (Pearson correlations of hepcidin with other markers within non-survivors; marker-marker correlations, not marker-severity). All 14 markers were also compared with 32 healthy controls (not extracted); no marker was compared only between infected and healthy dogs, so skipped_infected_vs_healthy = 0.

severity_definitions.label: non-survivors vs survivors
severity_definitions.definition: Infected dogs followed up during the treatment period for survival; died vs survived. No fixed follow-up horizon stated.
severity_definitions.quote: All the infected dogs were followed up during the treatment period for their survivability and they were classified into survivors (n=18) and non-survivors (n=14) of infection.

associations.statistic: one-way ANOVA with Tukey's test; group values shown only in Fig 1
associations.quote: Serum hepcidin concentration was found to be significantly higher (P<0.01) in non-survivors than in survivors and control groups (Fig 1).

The receiver operating characteristics curve analysis identified the prognostic cut-off value of hepcidin as 32.32 ng/mL with 100.00% specificity and 92.86% sensitivity. The area under the curve of hepcidin was about 0.984 at the confidence interval of 86.30% and 100.00% (P<0.01) and the Youden’s index was 0.928 (Fig 6).
associations.location: Results and discussion, last para; Fig 6
associations.note: Confidence interval printed as percentages ('86.30% and 100.00%'), copied as printed.

associations.marker_as_reported: Babesia species (B. vogeli, B. gibsoni, mixed infection)
associations.statistic: non-survivors: 3 B. gibsoni, 11 mixed; survivors: 8 B. vogeli, 9 B. gibsoni, 1 mixed; mortality 25% in B. gibsoni, 91.6% in mixed infection
associations.quote: Among the 14 non-survivors, 3 dogs had B. gibsoni infection and 11 dogs had mixed infection of B. gibsoni and B. vogeli . Out of 18 survivors, 8 dogs had B. vogeli infection, 9 dogs had B. gibsoni infection and 1 dog had a mixed infection of both.
associations.note: Direction refers to mixed B. gibsoni + B. vogeli infection (more frequent in non-survivors); no deaths with B. vogeli alone. No statistical test.
